# Market Research

## Overview
This page compiles internal market research and [competitive analysis](./competitive-analysis.md) for [Aurora Labs](./aurora-labs.md), specifically focusing on Q3 2026. It evaluates garden and soil [sensors](./sensors.md), kitchen and lifestyle adjacent products, competitive battlecard strategies, and ongoing [documentation](./documentation.md) discrepancies.

## Key Details

### Garden / Soil Sensors Comparison
The following table outlines specifications for Aurora Labs and its competitors in the garden and soil sensor market:

| Vendor | Product | Mesh | Cloud | Waterproof | Battery |
|--------|---------|------|-------|------------|---------|
| Aurora Labs | [Nova Widget](./nova-widget.md) | MeshSync | optional | IP54 | CR2032 |
| [SenseNode SN-400](./sensenode-sn-400.md) | SN-400 | [LoRaWAN](./lorawan.md) | required | IP67 | CR2450 |
| CheapoCo | SoilStick | WiFi | required | none | USB |

### Kitchen / Lifestyle (Adjacent) Products
Adjacent lifestyle products and their [protocols](./protocols.md):

| Vendor | Product | Protocol | Notes |
|--------|---------|----------|-------|
| [TeaBuddy](./teabuddy.md) | Puck | [BLE](./ble.md) | local-only tea timer |
| TimerCap | KS failed 2024 | mechanical | not smart |

### Competitive Battlecard Updates
- **SenseNode:** Sales and marketing should emphasize their ongoing subscription cost over a 3-year period.
- **TeaBuddy:** Classified as a non-competitor; positioning should focus on partnership and co-marketing opportunities only.

## Contradictions
&gt; **Contradiction:** An internal Amazon draft stated that the Nova Widget uses a CR2450 battery, whereas the official product specifications list it as a CR2032 battery. This discrepancy must be fixed before publication.
